slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: reviews love the glow/habit loop, but the product reads as a gadget to people who don't know they're dehydrated - the selling feature can't be felt through a screen [R1][R3].
Solution: Glow Up Hydration - live hydration-check stations, 7-day glow challenges, desk-worker targeting, giftable bundles.
45-day goal: 200 orders, 800 captures, +12 pts 'the bottle that reminds you' [O1-O3].
slides.notes: We sell the finish line, not the craft.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Smart water bottle: LED glow reminders, app-tracked intake, $60-70 bottles + accessories [S1].
The demo is the feature: the bottle lights up in your hand - judges see the glow, not a spec sheet [R1].
Reviews: 'glow'/'reminder' dominate - the light IS the habit loop [R1].
Sold DTC online; quantified-self wearable category [S3].
slides.notes: Hold the bottle up as the LED glows - 'this light just told me to drink. That's the whole product.'

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Smart hydration brand - 150+ verified reviews, wearable-adjacent positioning [S1][S2][S3].
Hydration tracking is a real gap: people track steps/sleep but forget water - the last untracked habit [R3][S3].
Positioning gap: 'fitness gadget' is cluttered; 'the bottle that reminds you' is unclaimed.
Campaign claims the reminder.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 200 attributed orders via GLOW15 + station QR at ~$60 AOV [O1].
O2: 800 email/SMS captures from stations + glow challenge [O2].
O3: 1.1M impressions; +12 pts 'the bottle that reminds you' on pre/post survey (n=150 + holdout) [O3].
Baseline: current list; week-0 survey; Shopify code report.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1: health-tracking achievers 18-34 - quantified-self users who track everything except water; gyms/campuses [S3][S4].
P2: desk workers + gifters 25-45 - forget water at desk; gift-occasion buyers [R3][R4].
P1 is the quantified-self story; P2 is reliable revenue.

slides.title: Research Methodology & Results
bullets: Content analysis of 150 public Judge.me reviews (collected 2026-11-07), keyword-coded [R1-R4].
Digital shelf audit of 8 sources: product pages, bundles, wearable-category positioning [S1][S3][S5].
Pending: intercept survey (n=150) at stations + 3 interviews - field kit ready.
Reviews prove the glow works; the gap is people who don't know they need it.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] 'Glow/reminder' dominate -> sell the light, not the bottle: 'the bottle that reminds you'.
[R2] App friction is the complaint -> demo the glow first (no app needed to see it).
[R3] Buyers had a stated health problem -> recruit problem-aware desk workers + trackers.
[R4] Strong gift mentions -> giftable bundle program for P2.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: Glow Up Hydration - the light reminds you; the campaign reminds them.
Push-pull: stations create the live glow demo (pull); challenge + gift drops convert at home (push) [R3][A4].
Quantified self as proof: intake numbers become shareable results [S3].
PESO: paid geo-social, earned gym/office PR, shared glow clips, owned email/SMS + challenge.
